name: tiny
notes: NOT A MEASUREMENT PROFILE. It exists for the loadtest end-to-end lane (MOTIR-8682) only: a few clients per role for under two minutes against two local `next start` processes, Postgres and k6 sharing one CI runner. Its numbers mean nothing about any server, and no report made from it is ever a baseline for a real run.
12 clients per instance: 9 agents (3 read · 2 write · 2 claim · 2 run) and 3 readers (1 tab holding the Workbench stream · 2 browsers).
TIMING — ramp 20 s, steady 60 s, ramp-down 5 s. readerBrowseThinkSeconds 1 so every reader route is visited inside the window; runs.agentSeconds 10 so several run lifecycles complete.
SHAPE — the smoke floor of 2 agent workspaces; 4 users, each a member of both with one token per role, mint 8 agents per role. The burst is 10 calls by 1 agent, 10 s into the steady window.

THRESHOLDS ARE LOOSE ON PURPOSE (targetRps 1, read p95 10 s, error rate 20 %): the lane asserts that every section of the report exists and every k6-backed reading was taken, never that a shared runner is fast.

GENERATOR LIMITS ARE AT THE SCHEMA'S MAXIMUM (cpuMeanMax 1, cpuPeakMax 1): the runner that plays the generator also hosts both app processes, Postgres and k6, so a busy runner must not turn the verdict INVALID. The report's rule is unchanged for real profiles.
